newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Moslem party boosted by rivals.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Moslem party boosted by rivals.

text.p: Tens of thousands of opposition supporters brought the streets of Jakarta to a standstill on Sunday, highlighting an alliance between Indonesia's Moslem-based minority party and loyalists of charismatic opposition figurehead Megawati Sukarnoputri.

Chanting "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greater) and displaying pictures of Megawati, the supporters gathered at a campaign rally for the May 29 general elections and then toured through the city in convoys of motorcycles, buses and trucks.
Riot police watched silently, despite an order not to allow political party supporters to carry portraits of leaders, and there was no violence.

Pictures of Megawati, the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), and the chairman of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP), Ismail Hasan Metareum, were seen in abundance.
"Long live PPP. Long Live Mega-Bintang," shouted the screaming supporters clad in green shirts, the PPP colour. The star, or bintang, is the PPP symbol.
"Mega-Bintang, you are the best," read one banner written in English displayed at the rally.
The PPP and the PDI are battling the much-larger ruling Golkar party for 425 elected seats in the 500-member parliament. The rest of the seats are allocated for the military, which does not vote.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.

Megawati, the daughter of Indonesia's founding president Sukarno, was ousted from the PDI leadership by a government-backed faction last year and she has been barred from participating in the elections. She had asked her supporters not to take part in the campaign but appears to have tacitly approved their alliance with the PPP.
Police have said they had arrested a number of people for carrying pictures of Megawati in previous rallies.

"Carrying pictures of individuals during the campaign is not allowed under the existing general election law," police spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Edward Aritonang was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying on Saturday
The agency gave no further details, and there were no reports of police confiscating Megawati pictures during Sunday's rally.

"I can say that many of the people who turned up here are supporters of Megawati. I voted for PDI in the previous elections. I will vote for PPP now but I am still a PDI supporter. I just don't like Surjadi (the head of the government-backed faction)," said Wahyung, a young man who attended the rally.
PPP chairman Ismail Hasan Metarum told reporters after speaking at the rally that he did not see anything wrong with Megawati's supporters joining the campaign.
"It's their right so I am not doing anything. It's their right and I have to respect it," he said.
Metareum said there had not been any discussions within his party about the alliance.

Political analysts have said the alliance between the PPP and Megawati supporters is perhaps the most interesting feature of an otherwise lacklustre campaign, but stressed that it would have only a negligible effect on Golkar's fortunes. The ruling party is expected to easily retain its majority in parliament, they said.
